convertibility_reason: Uses only built-in iTEMA indicator. Simple entry/exit rules based on TEMA slope reversal. Fixed lot sizing. No external .mqh libraries for trading logic. All indicators and trade operations are standard MT5 API calls.

derived_values.name: dtema2 - TEMA slope on previous bar (bar[2] - bar[3])
dtema1 - TEMA slope on current bar (bar[1] - bar[2])

other_exits: Close long when TEMA slope dtema1 becomes positive (slope turns upward), close short when TEMA slope dtema1 becomes negative (slope turns downward) - this is a momentum-based stop, not a reversal entry

custom_logic_notes: Multi-currency EA supporting up to 12 symbols simultaneously (0-11). Each symbol has independent parameters (symbol, trade enable flag, TEMA period, applied price, SL, TP, lots, slippage). Entry logic: long when previous-bar TEMA slope was positive and current-bar slope turns negative (slope reversal from up to down is actually a SELL signal - wait, re-reading: dtema2>0 && dtema1<0 means slope was positive 2 bars ago and turned negative 1 bar ago = DnSignal (sell). Conversely dtema2<0 && dtema1>0 = UpSignal (buy). This is a TEMA slope reversal strategy. Exit logic: UpStop fires when dtema1>0 (slope positive, close long since momentum may be turning), DnStop fires when dtema1<0 (slope negative, close short). SL/TP values are in points (not pips): StLoss=1000 points = 100 pips for 5-digit, TkProfit=2000 points = 200 pips for 5-digit. The digit adjustment uses SYMBOL_DIGITS+4 for NormalizeDouble rounding but does NOT multiply SL/TP by 10 for 5-digit brokers - SL/TP are already in point units via SymbolInfoDouble(SYMBOL_POINT) multiplication.
python_conversion_notes: Straightforward conversion. TEMA is available in most Python TA libraries (e.g., ta.trend.EMAIndicator applied 3 times, or pandas_ta.tema). The slope reversal logic (dtema2 vs dtema1) is simple: compare consecutive TEMA differences to detect sign changes. SL/TP are point-based using symbol point value - convert to price distances in Python. Multi-symbol support can be handled by iterating over a list of symbol configs. Position gate checks for existing position before entry. The IsNewBar() function ensures signals are evaluated once per bar - implement equivalent bar-change detection. Note: NormalizeDouble with Digits_+4 is used for floating-point comparison precision, not for SL/TP calculation - use np.round or similar in Python.
